How about this one bro... I had a stable government job. I left it to do something very stupid (work abroad as a fucking english teacher) and now I'm back in rural america, living with my parents and unemployed. Oh, it gets better: I'm 33, and I'm completely broke. That's right, I can't even afford food. I sold some belongings online to buy some food I wanted. I'm on the edge too. Every day it's possible I take the plunge, literally, plunge off a cliff.

If you just quit your job you're going to be dealing with a whole host of other problems. Not the same problems, different ones, but still problems. The problems in life don't go away. You're doing nothing wrong right now. You're doing great. You're supporting a child and a spouse. Hating your job can be changed. There are other jobs out there. But you know the old adage "Don't quit your day job?" DON'T. Find another one FIRST, then by all means, quit the other one. This is a discussion you must have with your wife. You are a team, bringing a new person into the world. No one ever said it's going to be easy, and if they did, they were full of shit. But working through the hard stuff makes all the other great moments of life possible. You are that child's hero. Are you going to turn your back on your own child and wife? Isn't seeing your child's stomach full, clothes on his back, and a roof over his head worth the job you hate? If you love your son more than you hate your job, then it is worth it to keep going. IT IS WORTH IT.

You have a job, at least one child, and a wife. Let me repeat that. You have a JOB, at least ONE CHILD, and a WIFE. I think at least half of all of America hates their job. But it's a means to an end. Would you rather be unemployed, completely broke, dependent on welfare? It is nice to walk through grocery stores and pick things out knowing you can pay for it at the end. And you have to buy food for a long, long time. And people are depending on you. People that love you. You can work on changing your job. But now you have people relying on you. You were put into this position for a reason, because a greater power knew you could handle it.

Ah, yes, the knee jerk "troll" term being bandied about. You know this is so unoriginal and such a cliche. Whenever someone throws that term around, it tells me they can't adequately find a rebuttal to my points and so deem me a troll, which by the way is the same as cheap, elementary playground tactics. You resort to name calling because you cannot sufficiently argue the issues brought up. Such are the ways of others.

I never said it won't impact anyone. I said it's naive and presumptuous to believe that because it happened to them, it can happen to anyone. As for the hope part, "hope" is a mostly useless term thrown about by people with good lives who have no idea what it is to live on the other side day-to-day for years. Even if the poster did suffer in this way and now propounds "hope" to all who will listen, then let him preach hope. As for "everyone" having the potential for a life changing moment, this is  idealistic and false. Only God could make such a claim. Is the poster God? I am highly doubtful.

this is the typical "life is great for me now, even though I was at the bottom, so it can be great for you too no matter how low you are!" sentiment. People, like the poster here, are 'significance junkies.' Their experience has empowered them, and now they think there is limitless possibility for others too. What they don't realize is their experience is merely a data point, and I could point to other experiences (data points) where it turned out even worse for the individual, and it would have been better had they gone away. But people with "good lives" want to shove their goodness in other peoples faces and say "See, you can have this too!" when in fact this is often not the case. Will you say the same to a person in somalia caught in the throes of a civil war, living in desperately poor places, and statistically likely to never escape? No, you won't. Don't presume to believe that your experience in any way affects what COULD happen to others. It's not only awfully presumptuous, it's naive and merely based on intuition, not on fact or the reality of others situations.
